description: Golden reference for the calc_fem_kelvin -> calc_heat chain (Phase B end-to-end).
rationale: Locks two things: (1) calc_fem_kelvin still emits qsurf.sol on the EM mesh with the documented .sol layout, and (2) calc_heat's per-vertex cross-mesh projection still hits the same physical surface so that integrating q_surf over the workpiece thermal mesh matches calc_fem_kelvin's P_total within mesh-interpolation noise.  This is the regression catcher for the spatial-Q pipeline as a whole; the calc_heat solver itself is also exercised here via a uniform-Q smoke run that the panel can fall back to.

sample.geometry_match_note: wp_vol fixture is a cylinder R=0.025 H=0.025 centered on Z=0, MIRRORING the workpiece subtracted from the IH sample.  Surface-vertex projection should hit 100% of the EM SIBC face.

notes: Test current I=1.0 A is for fingerprint reproducibility, not realistic IH operation.  Heat values scale as I^2 so any future user runs at kA currents will get realistic T.

tolerance_temp_K is in absolute Kelvin (1e-5) because the temperature rise itself is ~5e-6 K -- an absolute bracket is the right scale.  For high-current production runs the relative tolerance becomes irrelevant.

q_surf_int W: the integral over the THERMAL surface of the projected q_surf field.  Differs from P_total_W (the EM-side surface integral) by ~1-2% because of cross-mesh interpolation between two different surface mesh densities.  This is the headline cross-mesh-transfer correctness check.
